tokenizer: ordinary o200k_base, same warmed Retok protocol input_tokens for ALL arms
timing: one unmeasured warmup per arm; rotating order; subprocess wall time; no audit shims
protocol_timing: warmed compact request round trip, excludes startup, includes JSON/pipe overhead
candidate_status: Development release-mode Retok v0.2.0 binary, not a shipped artifact; final source/release qualification pending
environment: Linux shared host; governed run; warm filesystem caches; no host identity recorded here
limitations: Seven predeclared modest synthetic workloads and three controls; no aggregate winner or model-task/billing conclusion.
One warmup per arm; five timed repeats; order rotates; startup, subprocess work and normal local tracking included.
Warm processing is separate Retok protocol round-trip time, including Python JSON/pipe overhead; not runner CPU time or RTK processing time.
Same warmed Retok ordinary o200k_base tokenizer counts actual stdout and stderr separately for every arm; no independent tiktoken verification.
Untimed PATH audit observes native child argv/cwd/count; internal or absolute-path execution is not fully observable.
Content hashes include Git metadata; no claim about access timestamps, identical rewrites, every subprocess or external side effect.
Text restore is byte-exact; JSON uses independent Python Number lexemes and typed parsed values, permitting whitespace/key-order changes.
Runner output must equal the exact saved original or the exact explicit-encoding protocol candidate per stream.
Runner bypasses streams below 256 bytes; progress may stream raw. RTK controls use proxy, not output filters.
Literal marker absence is not semantic loss by itself, particularly for reversible encoding.
Memory, first-byte progress latency, TTY behavior and agent outcomes are not measured.
Native long listing contains runtime owner/group names; only token counts/hashes are published, so counts can vary across systems.
